decisions.evidence: Round 3, entries 5–6: maker proposes “a short readable title that I generate from the link's address”; client instead expects “the page’s real title, a short description, and its small site icon automatically.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the proposed metadata collection differed from the reference, and the client supplied the conforming behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 3, entries 5–6: maker says each item shows only a site-name chip, generated title, and full link; client requests the real title, description, and site icon and says the source chip must not resemble a user tag.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the initial card omitted reference readability fields; the client corrected its content and visual distinction.

decisions.evidence: Round 3, entries 5–6: the prototype saves directly; client asks to “correct the title or description before saving and edit them later.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client added the missing before/after metadata-editing requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 3, entries 5–6: duplicate handling is absent from the presented saving flow; client says an already-saved link must not duplicate and should open the existing bookmark for updating.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client added the missing duplicate-save convergence rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 3, entries 5–6: maker sets newest saves at the top; client says “newest-first is a sensible default.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: this is a conforming sort choice.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, entries 7–8: maker presents editable title/description in a pre-save review panel and later editing; client says all three actions behave as expected.
decisions.note: Revised prototype review: title and description can be corrected before and after saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, entries 7–8: re-entering the same link opens and highlights the existing bookmark for updating; client says this “feels right.”
decisions.note: Revised prototype review: duplicate saves conform to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, entries 7–8: maker presents gathered title, description, and site icon but no preview image; client adds that the finished version should collect the page’s preview image when available.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client identified the remaining missing metadata field.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, entries 7–8: maker limits later editing to “title or description”; client generally approves later editing without identifying the missing URL, tags, and note fields.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the edit scope was narrower than the reference and passed without an explicit response to that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 5, entries 9–10: maker adds the collected preview image to review and card views with a text-only fallback when absent; client approves its size, position, and omission fallback.
decisions.note: Prototype review: preview collection and readable display conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 6, entries 11–12: all three variants allow adding multiple removable tags; client approves the tagging approach.
decisions.note: Prototype review: multi-tag assignment conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 6, entries 11–12: maker offers type-only, comma-separated, and existing-tag suggestion variants; client selects Version 3 because tapping existing tags is faster and prevents near-duplicates.
decisions.note: Prototype review: offered alternatives differed in autocomplete fulfillment, and the client selected the conforming one.

decisions.evidence: Round 6, entries 11–12: maker displays tags beneath the description as distinct pills; client says they are clear, well placed, and unlike source information.
decisions.note: Prototype review: assigned tags are exposed readably per item.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entries 13–14: typing narrows existing-tag suggestions while Enter can create a new tag; client says the interaction feels natural.
decisions.note: Prototype review: autocomplete remains available alongside new-tag creation.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, entries 15–16: maker explicitly excludes the raw link address from search; client says “please include the full link address too.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client replaced the incomplete full-text field set with the reference-conforming scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, entries 15–16: case handling is absent from the presented search behavior; client states “Search should also ignore capitalisation.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client supplied the missing case-insensitivity rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, entries 15–16: maker presents ordinary word search only; client requests “`#recipes` for a tag.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client added the missing tag-search syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, entries 15–16: maker presents simple all-words matching; client requests `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, grouped expressions, and quoted operator words treated literally.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client added the missing Boolean grammar and literal-operator rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, entries 15–16: exact-phrase syntax is absent; client requests quotation marks for an exact phrase.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client added the missing quoted-phrase behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, entries 15–16: maker makes two ordinary words require both; client says that is what they expect.
decisions.note: Prototype review: ordinary terms combine with narrowing/AND semantics.

decisions.evidence: Round 9, entry 17: maker demonstrates that a word appearing only in the full web address is found.
decisions.note: Revised prototype review: full-text search now includes the URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 9, entries 17–18: maker makes `#tag` a contains-match, such that `#rec` finds `recipes`; client requires `#recipes` to match only that specific tag.
decisions.note: Prototype review: loose tag-query matching differed from specific-tag filtering, and the client corrected it.

decisions.evidence: Round 9, entry 17: maker demonstrates grouped Boolean queries, NOT, and quoted `“AND”` as literal text.
decisions.note: Revised prototype review: Boolean, grouping, and quoted-operator behavior conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 9, entry 17: maker demonstrates `“async rust”` as an exact phrase.
decisions.note: Revised prototype review: quoted phrase matching conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, entries 19–20: maker assumes every saved bookmark starts in the Reading list; client says reference links should not and requires deliberate read-later marking.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the default unread model contradicted the opt-in read-later state, and the client corrected it.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, entries 19–20: maker sends a bookmark marked read into Archive; client requires marking read to remove it from Reading list while keeping it in the main collection.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the read transition was corrected to the reference behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, entries 19–20: maker stores both read and explicitly archived items together in Archive and restores them to Reading list; client requires Archive to contain only explicitly archived items, hidden from active views and restorable to Collection.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client corrected the archive model and its distinction from read state.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, entries 19–20: search stays within the current tab, with archived material searched only in Archive; client explicitly retains this scoped-search rule.
decisions.note: Prototype review: archive search isolation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 11, entries 21–22: new saves remain in Collection, Add to reading list is explicit, and Mark as read removes only the unread flag; client says the separation is correct.
decisions.note: Revised prototype review: the read-later lifecycle conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 11, entries 21–22: Archive hides bookmarks from Collection and ordinary search, has its own search, and supports restoration; client approves the separation.
decisions.note: Revised prototype review: archive behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 12, entries 23–24: maker adds an optional save-time read-later flag while preserving later changes; client says this matches the intended light choice.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the bookmark can be deliberately marked read-later during or after saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 13, entries 25–26: non-link input is declined without saving; client approves the invalid-link response.
decisions.note: Prototype review: URL-required saving conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 13, entries 25–26: maker presents long content wrapping, a clean bare bookmark, and favicon letter fallbacks; client confirms none break the card layout.
decisions.note: Prototype review: list presentation remains readability-first across edge cases.

decisions.evidence: Round 13, entries 25–26: maker says “nothing is ever truly deleted” and only Archive exists; client requires permanent Delete as a separate confirmed action while Archive remains reversible.
decisions.note: Prototype review: absence of permanent deletion contradicted the reference and was corrected.

decisions.evidence: Round 14, entries 27–28: maker adds permanent Delete with an irreversible-warning confirmation, separate from reversible Archive; client says they now feel properly distinct.
decisions.note: Revised prototype review: deletion and archiving conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, entries 29–30: the purportedly complete summary says search covers “title, your notes, tags, site name, and the full address” but omits page description; the client lists other unfinished features without surfacing this omission.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the summarized search field set was incomplete, and this difference passed unexpressed at this stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, entries 29–30: the summary mentions editing title and description only; client says address, tags, and personal note must also be editable.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client added the missing edit fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, entries 29–30: a separate rendered markdown note is absent from the purportedly complete baseline; client requires a personal note distinct from description, with simple formatting and rendered display.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client added the missing markdown-note requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, entries 29–30: opening the original page is absent from the complete summary; client asks for clicking a bookmark to open it.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client added the missing original-URL navigation behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, entries 29–30: direct tag filtering is absent from the complete summary; client asks for clicking a tag to filter the collection by that tag.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client added the missing tag-filter action.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, entries 29–30: sorting is absent from the complete summary; client asks for sorting by date added or title.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client added the missing sorting capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, entries 29–30: bulk selection/actions are absent; client requests selecting several bookmarks and bulk tag, read/unread, archive, and delete operations.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client added the missing multi-select bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, entries 29–30: no whole-filter result action is summarized; client explicitly requests selecting “all bookmarks in the current search or view.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client added the missing all-matching bulk scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, entries 29–30: reusable saved filters are absent; client asks to save a useful search and its included or excluded tags.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client added the missing bundle/saved-filter behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, entries 29–30: page preservation is absent; client asks to keep a saved page copy and the original PDF for PDF URLs.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client added the missing local snapshot/PDF behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, entries 29–30: Internet Archive support is absent; client says saving to the Internet Archive would be useful.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client added the missing Internet Archive option.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, entries 29–30: import is absent; client requires importing browser bookmarks without losing titles, tags, or original saved dates.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client added the missing Netscape-style import requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, entries 29–30: export is absent; client requires exporting browser bookmarks without losing titles, tags, or saved dates.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client added the missing export requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, entries 29–30: personal display settings are absent; client requests default sorting, displayed-item count, and text size.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client added the missing display settings.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 16–17, entries 31–34: maker presents a separate markdown-backed note and rendered card block; client initially defers visual judgment, then accepts after the corrected card shows description and rendered note distinctly.
decisions.note: Linked prototype-review sequence: the clarification was resolved without double-counting; the final presented behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 16, entries 31–32: maker adds address and tag editing alongside title, description, and note editing; client says the shared Edit panel matches the need.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the full bookmark edit scope conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 18, entries 35–36: title and preview image open the original URL in a new tab; client approves those targets.
decisions.note: Prototype review: selecting the item navigates to the original URL through functionally appropriate targets.

decisions.evidence: Round 18, entries 35–36: maker makes every tag click jump to Collection; client requires the tag filter to stay within Collection, Reading list, or Archive, especially so archived tagged items remain visible.
decisions.note: Prototype review: tag filtering broke the current perspective, and the client supplied the conforming scoped behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 19, entries 37–38: maker keeps tag filtering in the current view and exposes the exact `#tag` filter; client confirms this is the desired behavior.
decisions.note: Revised prototype review: specific-tag filtering conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 20, entries 39–40: maker offers newest, oldest, recently updated, and both title directions; client says the set covers their needs.
decisions.note: Prototype review: list sorting conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 21, entries 41–42: maker presents multi-select with add/remove tags, read/unread, archive/restore, and confirmed delete; client says the action set is complete.
decisions.note: Prototype review: multi-bookmark bulk actions conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 21, entries 41–42: maker labels the scope “Select all … shown” and describes everything currently shown; client corrects this to every bookmark matching the current view and search, not merely visible cards.
decisions.note: Prototype review: visible-page selection differed from whole-filter selection, and the client corrected the scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 22, entries 43–44: maker saves a named search with its words and included/excluded tags for reuse; client approves the saved-search behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the saved filter/bundle conforms; remembering the view is an additional compatible choice.

decisions.evidence: Round 23, entries 45–46: maker offers manual versus automatic local copies and currently uses a per-bookmark manual action; client selects automatic creation whenever a bookmark is saved.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the offered alternatives differed from on-save preservation, and the client selected the reference-conforming option.

decisions.evidence: Round 23, entries 45–46: maker refers generically to a stored page copy without the single-file rule; client specifies “a single self-contained page file.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client supplied the missing snapshot-format rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 23, entries 45–46: maker keeps the PDF itself for PDF URLs; client explicitly confirms that behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: PDF snapshot handling conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 23, entries 45–46: maker provides Internet Archive saving independently from the app-held copy; client retains it as a separate manual choice.
decisions.note: Prototype review: Internet Archive support conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 24, entries 47–48: maker revises to automatic local page/PDF copies, refreshable locally, with manual Internet Archive submission; client says this matches the requirement.
decisions.note: Revised prototype review: snapshot and Internet Archive behavior conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 25, entries 49–50: maker imports browser HTML while preserving title, tags, and original saved date, previews it, and skips duplicate URLs; client approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: Netscape-format import fulfills the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 25, entries 49–50: maker exports browser-compatible HTML with title, `TAGS`, and `ADD_DATE`; client values the portable export.
decisions.note: Prototype review: Netscape-format export conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 26, entries 51–52: maker presents remembered default sort, displayed-item limit, and Small/Normal/Large text size; client approves and requires persistence between visits.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the specified personal display settings conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 26, entries 51–52: maker demonstrates that search and Select all cover the full matching set despite a display limit; client approves that proviso.
decisions.note: Revised prototype review: all-matching bulk scope now conforms across loaded and unloaded items.

decisions.evidence: Round 27, entries 53–54: the final baseline again lists title, note, tags, site name, and full address but omits page description; client grants implementation approval only “with one correction” that page description must also be searched.
decisions.note: Final specification gate: the client explicitly surfaced and corrected the incomplete search scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 28, entries 55–56: maker’s implementation report explicitly says the full search language includes page description; client accepts and notes the corrected search scope.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the revised presented search scope conforms.
